problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{3}$
- $AC=CA={I}_{3}$
- $B={A}^{-1}$

examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Inverse of a Larger Matrix
examples.problem:
Using the method of direct verification, determine whether the matrix $B$ is the inverse of $A,$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we  check whether $AB = BA = I_3.$

Computing $AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $BA,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BA & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B = A^{-1}.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{2}$
- $AC=CA={I}_{2}$
- $B={A}^{-1}$
feedback.worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $AB=BA={I}_{2}.$ Computing $AB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}∗ & 6 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{2}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is false. As a result, $B\ne {A}^{-1}$ and statement III is false too.

- Now, we check whether $AC=CA={I}_{2}.$ Computing $AC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $CA$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CA & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
